topics.label: Course Overview and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening introduces the lecturer, sets the context for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the session's core learning objectives.

topics.label: Determinants of Cancer Risk: Genetics, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explore the interplay between endogenous cellular errors, inherited genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures demonstrated by epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how infectious agents such as bacteria, parasites, and viruses contribute to oncogenesis, highlighted by the detailed case study of Epstein-Barr virus and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Metabolic Activation and DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific physical and chemical mutagens—including dietary toxins, UV radiation, polycyclic hydrocarbons, and aromatic amines—cause DNA damage directly or via xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on the distinction between initiators and promoters, inflammation-driven tumor progression, and tissue vulnerability during specific developmental life stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific methods used to detect, test, and validate carcinogenicity, encompassing genomic mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo animal bioassays, and the in vitro Ames test.
